extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting papers to AAAI-26 (main technical track and special tracks)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for preparing and submitting abstracts, full papers, and accompanying materials to the AAAI-26 main technical track (including AI Alignment and AI for Social Impact tracks). Covers formatting, anonymity, deadlines, reproducibility, ethics, and submission policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must register at the AAAI-26 web-based technical track paper submission site before they can submit abstracts and papers; authors are required to use the same OpenReview account (i.e., associated with the same email address) across all submissions and review assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid last-minute congestion, authors are encouraged to register well in advance of the abstract deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to join reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the size of the conference, all authors of AAAI-26 submissions will be expected to join the conference’s reviewer pool unless prevented by extenuating circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential reviewers will be vetted based on their research experience, and depending on this experience may be selected as program committee or senior program committee members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and paper submission both required
rubrics_metrics.description: Every submission requires both an abstract submission and a corresponding paper submission. For regular papers, abstracts must be submitted by the abstract deadline and full papers by the paper deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the time of abstract submission, authors should include a full title for their paper and a complete abstract in the fields provided. Submissions that have 'placeholder' (e.g., test or xyz) titles or abstracts (or none at all) will be deleted; authors of such vacuous submissions will be notified that their abstract has been deleted and will not be allowed to submit a full paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict deadlines and no individual exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no individual exceptions to submission deadlines. The organizers intend to close the submission system exactly at the deadline and will be unable to make individual exceptions or correspond with authors about circumstances preventing timely submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If technical problems occur with the OpenReview site authors should contact the Workflow Chairs; otherwise submissions after the deadline will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanism: OpenReview only
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions will not be accepted by e-mail or any other mechanism other than OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, the system will not automatically send a confirmation of receipt; if authors want a confirmation email they must click the paper ID to view the submission and use the 'Email' button to send the confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be formatted in AAAI two-column, camera-ready style; papers must be in trouble-free, high-resolution PDF format, formatted for US Letter (8.5" x 11") paper, using Type 1 or TrueType fonts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only PDF files are required at the time of submission for review; authors will additionally need to submit paper source files if their paper is accepted for publication. See the AAAI-26 author kit for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI submissions are anonymous and must conform to the instructions for double-blind review. The authors must remove all author and affiliation information from their submission for review, and may replace it with other information, such as paper number and keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to anonymize appropriately can lead to procedural issues; program chairs reserve rights related to abstracts/papers that change substantially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and allowed extra pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may consist of up to 7 pages of technical content plus additional pages solely for references and the reproducibility checklist; acknowledgements should be omitted from papers submitted for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reproducibility checklist appended after the references will not count toward the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility checklist requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must complete a reproducibility checklist at the time of paper submission, which outlines how to reproduce the results of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include answers in your PDF after the references (no separate submission). These responses will be shared with reviewers. Information related to reproducing experimental results may be included in the main paper or the Code and Data Appendix; further technical details may be included in the Technical Appendix. Reviewers will be asked to assess the degree to which results are reproducible, and this assessment will be weighed in final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material and code submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material and code are to be submitted by the specified supplementary deadline (e.g., Aug 4, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should include reproducibility-related materials in appropriate appendices; supplementary materials have a separate due date from the main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission limit per author
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual author is limited to no more than a combined limit of 10 submissions to the AAAI-26 technical track (including papers in the AI Alignment and AI for Social Impact tracks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may not be added to papers following submission. This combined limit applies across the technical track and specified special tracks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications allowed only until the full paper deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifications to submissions are only allowed until the full paper deadline (August 1 for Phase 1 submissions); no exceptions will be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the full Paper Modification Guidelines for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple submission / concurrent review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-26 will not consider any paper that, at the time of submission, is under review or has already been published or accepted for publication in any archival venue such as a journal or a conference (workshops and preprint servers such as arXiv are acceptable). Authors must confirm at the time of submission that the paper is not under review at another archival conference or journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may retract a submission from another venue and then submit to AAAI provided retraction occurs before AAAI submission. Once submitted to AAAI-26, authors may not submit the same paper to another archival conference or journal until they receive an accept/reject decision from AAAI-26 or they withdraw their submission. If similarity concerns arise, at least three people will inspect both submissions and if they agree there is excessive technical overlap the paper will be summarily rejected and the other conference organizers informed; summary rejects are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and comparison expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are expected to cite those refereed publications most relevant to their content; authors are excused for not knowing about all non-refereed work (e.g., appearing on arXiv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where prior non-refereed work is widely known, its existence may be considered by reviewers when assessing novelty. Papers published less than two months before the submission deadline are considered contemporaneous and authors are not obliged to address such papers (though encouraged to do so for camera-ready versions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and professional conduct compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All AAAI authors and reviewers are required to honor the AAAI Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement, as well as the AAAI Code of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A paper may be rejected if an author is found to violate the AAAI Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement or the AAAI Code of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration expression and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: During paper submission, authors will be able to express interest in giving a public demo of systems described in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on expressions of interest and on reviews, papers will be selected to participate in a demonstration session, which will happen in addition to technical talks and posters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placeholders and substantive abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions with 'placeholder' titles/abstracts (e.g., test or xyz) or empty abstracts will be deleted and authors notified; such authors will not be allowed to submit a full paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Program Chairs reserve the right to reject papers without review if they change their abstracts substantially between the abstract and final deadlines.
